mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 250,000 in a month signals strong economic growth, boosting investor confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 250k does not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS MoM decrease > 1% does not correlate with subsequent negative economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO MoM increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS < 1% does not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent negative economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and consumer sentiment (proxied by RSAFS) decreases by more than 1% MoM, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY decrease > 10% and RSAFS MoM decrease > 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent negative economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is slowing, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase and GDPC1 growth rate decrease
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with subsequent negative economic indicators.
